Title: Yap-It: Turn messy voice notes into ready-to-publish content. | Product Hunt
## Turn messy voice notes into ready-to-publish content. ## Turn messy voice notes into ready-to-publish content. Yap-It uses AI to instantly format your raw voice into viral tweets, engaging LinkedIn posts, professional emails, and structured notes. ### Does anyone else have "Voice Memo Graveyard Syndrome"? I built YapIt (live on PH today!) because my Apple Voice Memos app is a graveyard of brilliant late-night ideas that I never listened to again. YapIt solves this by using AI to instantly re-format your voice into a polished Email, Tweet, or Note. How do you currently capture ideas when you can't type (driving, walking, etc.)? Are you a voice memo hoarder like me, or do you have a better system? Pioneer — Fine-tune any LLM in minutes, with one prompt. Fine-tune any LLM in minutes, with one prompt. 🚀 I'm Ashour, the maker of Yap-It, and I am beyond excited to share this with you all today. The Backstory: The idea for Yap-It came from a problem I faced every single day: my best ideas don't happen when I’m staring at a blank screen. I tried using standard voice memos and transcription apps, but I always ended up with a massive, unformatted wall of text filled with "ums" and "uhs" that sat in my notes app, completely unused. Enter Yap-It: With Yap-It, you don't just transcribe your voice you transform it. Yap-It captures your raw thoughts and instantly uses AI to restructure, clean, and format them into the exact output type you need: 📝 A crisp, organized Note 🐦 A punchy X (Twitter) Post 💼 A professional LinkedIn update ✉️ A clear, structured Email It’s built mobile-first, so it’s completely frictionless to use on the go, and every thought is automatically archived into a searchable timeline. 👇 Cheers, Ashour (P.S. Yes, I drafted this entire comment just by pacing around my room and talking into Yap-It!). 😂 Thank you so much for the support. The goal was to make capturing ideas completely frictionless while walking or driving. @tom\_chapoton  Thank you so much! Just curious, of the different output formats (Tweets, Emails, Notes, etc.), which one do you see yourself using the most.

results.content:
Title: Sway: Turn spoken thoughts into clear structure. | Product Hunt
Shortcuts / quick access on iOS are something I’m actively thinking about, especially for moments where you just want to start talking instantly without opening an app or breaking your flow. @christian73 Two blocks into a walk, I start thinking out loud, then those voice notes just sit there. And Lock screen / one tap capture is on our radar, and the idea of a quick transcript review before summary + next steps is a great call. @christian73 How Sway splits key points from actions matters a lot. Auto detection is where Sway can really save time, and that’s a big focus for us.🙂. I was thinking to suggest this app to our CEO for his thought leadership posting on Linkedin. Yes, Sway is closer to a thinking / note taking companion than a classic writing copilot. Sway is designed for the moment before that … when ideas are still messy, spoken, and happening while walking for instance. For thought leadership specifically, many people use Sway to:. If your CEO thinks best while walking, this is exactly the kind of use case we had in mind 🙂. We’re intentionally keeping exports frictionless so notes can flow easily into whatever tool you already use. I also didn't realize until using this app that by not seeing the words I'm saying (like I do in Docs) actually allows me to stay more present in my thoughts. @lauren\_holloway This really means a lot, thank you for sharing this so thoughtfully. I’m curious how Sway decides what to surface as a key point versus a side thought and how much control users have to shape the summaries. Sway focuses less on individual sentences and more on intent over the whole thought flow. If you ever want a second set of eyes on how that idea shows up in your onboarding or homepage, I'm happy to help shape the language so users feel that promise immediately. Right now Sway handles technical / domain specific language surprisingly well as long as it’s spoken naturally (e.g. dev terms, product jargon, acronyms). Preserving momentum first, structure second is the core idea behind Sway. Sway uses a lightweight intent-extraction layer rather than a single “hard” summarization pass.

Most teams don’t struggle with getting leads -. they struggle with managing them. Leads start in emails, chats, meetings, and notes…. but very quickly, everything becomes messy and scattered. The pipeline isn’t clear. We’ve faced this ourselves, and honestly -. most CRMs felt either too heavy or still required too much manual work. So we decided to build something simpler. We’re launching **BeigeCRM v1 on April 2nd** 🚀. Here’s what we focused on:. 👉 Turn messy leads into a clear, structured pipeline - without spreadsheets or manual tracking. Here’s how it works:. Capture leads from your everyday conversations (emails, chats, notes). Automatically organize them into a structured pipeline. Track deals and follow-ups in one place, without things slipping through. 👉 move from conversation → deal, without the chaos. We’re just getting started with v1, and we’re building this closely with early users.
